name: Discrete Volume Rendering Integral
definition: The volume rendering integral is discretized into a summation over sample points along a ray, assuming a zero background intensity ($I_0 = 0$). The ray $r$ is parameterized by $ho_r( ar{ho}) :  ar{R} ightarrow  ar{R}^2$, entering the volume at $ ar{ho} = 0$ and exiting at $ ar{ho} = D$. The data model is sampled using $s( ar{ho})$. summary: The Discrete Volume Rendering Integral approximates the continuous rendering equation using Riemann sums, distinguishing itself from analytical and higher-order methods by assuming constant density and color within each discretized ray segment.
